tagline: A loop out of the town Roosevelt renamed.
intro: From Warm Springs the loop runs north on State Route 85 to Gay, then east on Flat Shoals Road across the Flint River and down State Route 18 to Molena. It comes back through Manchester, a railroad town under Pine Mountain, and returns to Warm Springs on State Route 190 along the ridge. At Jones Mill a grist mill and its pond are all that remain of a farm community.

Warm Springs was a spa town called Bullochville when Franklin Roosevelt first came in 1924 to exercise his weakened legs in water that holds at 88 degrees. He kept coming back for two decades, and he renamed the town.

moments.title: Little White House
moments.text: Roosevelt had this six-room Georgia pine house built in 1932 and died here in April 1945, while Elizabeth Shoumatoff was painting the portrait that still hangs unfinished.

moments.title: Red Oak Creek Covered Bridge
moments.text: North of Woodbury a lattice bridge probably built around 1840 by Horace King, an enslaved man, crosses Red Oak Creek, held together by some 2,500 wooden pegs.

moments.title: Gay
moments.text: A town of about 110 people that draws thousands every May and October to a cotton fair it has held since 1972.
